King Parīkṣit said: My dear lord, you have elaborately described the dynasties of both the moon-god and the sun-god, with the exalted and wonderful character of their kings.
reflection: When I hear about Kṛṣṇa's appearance in the Yadu dynasty, do I treat it as ancient history or as a confidential subject I am personally meant to penetrate — and what specifically have I done this week to penetrate it?

snippet: O best of munis, you have also described the descendants of Yadu, who were very pious and strictly adherent to religious principles. Now, if you will, kindly describe the wonderful, glorious activities of Lord Viṣṇu,…
reflection: When I sit to hear about Kṛṣṇa, am I actually hungry for His personal vīryāṇi, or am I settling for moral lessons and 'pious dynasty' content that leaves Him at a safe distance?

snippet: The Supersoul, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the cause of the cosmic manifestation, appeared in the dynasty of Yadu. Please tell me elaborately about His glorious activities and character, from the…
reflection: When I retell or remember Kṛṣṇa's pastimes, where do I notice my mind reducing Him to symbol or principle rather than meeting Him as the supremely attractive person in Vraja?

snippet: Glorification of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is performed in the paramparā system, that is, it is conveyed from the spiritual master to disciple. Such glorification is relished by those no longer interested in…
reflection: When kṛṣṇa-kathā is being spoken, where does my mind drift first — and what does that drift reveal about the 'temporary glorification' I am still relishing?

snippet: Taking the boat of Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet, my grandfather Arjuna and others crossed the ocean of the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra, in which such commanders as Bhīṣmadeva resembled great fish that could very easily have…
reflection: When I face my own Kurukṣetra — a relationship, illness, or career battle that feels populated by Bhīṣma-sized fish — do I actually take shelter of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, or do I only invoke Him decoratively while paddling with my own strength?

snippet: My dear Śukadeva Gosvāmī, you have already explained that Saṅkarṣaṇa, who belongs to the second quadruple, appeared as the son of Rohiṇī named Balarāma. If Balarāma was not transferred from one body to another, how…
reflection: Where do I quietly assume the body is the self — treating my own changes of body, role, or station as if they were transfers of *me* — and how would I act differently today if I held Balarāma's truth that the soul does not migrate even when the vessel does?

snippet: Why did Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, leave the house of His father, Vasudeva, and transfer Himself to the house of Nanda in Vṛndāvana? Where did the Lord, the master of the Yadu dynasty, live with His…
reflection: Where in my own life have I been clinging to the 'house of Vasudeva' — a setting of formal reverence and security — when Kṛṣṇa is actually inviting me into the more intimate, demanding sevā of Vraja?

snippet: Lord Kṛṣṇa lived both in Vṛndāvana and in Mathurā. What did He do there? Why did He kill Kaṁsa, His mother’s brother? Such killing is not at all sanctioned in the śāstras.
reflection: Where in my life am I treating a familial or social tie — like Kaṁsa being Kṛṣṇa's maternal uncle — as a reason to tolerate behavior that is actually demonic, and what is that tolerance costing the souls around me?

snippet: Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, has no material body, yet He appears as a human being. For how many years did He live with the descendants of Vṛṣṇi? How many wives did He marry, and for how many years did…
reflection: Where am I quietly treating Kṛṣṇa as merely a great human, an inspiring teacher, or a formless 'consciousness' — and what specifically would change in my sādhana today if I held Him as sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha, narākṛti, personally present?

snippet: O great sage, who know everything about Kṛṣṇa, please describe in detail all the activities of which I have inquired and also those of which I have not, for I have full faith and am very eager to hear of them.
reflection: Where in my hearing of Kṛṣṇa's līlā am I quietly filtering — accepting the parts that flatter my reason and skipping the ones that strain my śraddhā?

snippet: Because of my vow on the verge of death, I have given up even drinking water, yet because I am drinking the nectar of topics about Kṛṣṇa, which is flowing from the lotus mouth of your Lordship, my hunger and thirst,…
reflection: When my body's hunger, thirst, fatigue, or restlessness flares up, do I treat it as proof that hari-kathā must wait — or do I test whether deeper absorption in Kṛṣṇa's topics actually quiets the demand, the way Parīkṣit Mahārāja's fast became weightless in Śukadeva's presence?

snippet: Sūta Gosvāmī said: O son of Bhṛgu, after Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the most respectable devotee, the son of Vyāsadeva, heard the pious questions of Mahārāja Parīkṣit, he thanked the King with great respect. Then he began to…
reflection: Where in my life am I still seeking remedies for kali-kalmaṣa — anxiety, restlessness, lifelessness — in places other than kṛṣṇa-kathā, and what does that misplaced trust cost me each day?

snippet: Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O Your Majesty, best of all saintly kings, because you are greatly attracted to topics of Vāsudeva, it is certain that your intelligence is firmly fixed in spiritual understanding, which…
reflection: Where in my day am I starving my intelligence of vāsudeva-kathā and feeding it instead on news, gossip, or strategy — and what does that diet reveal about where my buddhi is actually 'firmly fixed'?

snippet: The Ganges, emanating from the toe of Lord Viṣṇu, purifies the three worlds, the upper, middle and lower planetary systems. Similarly, when one asks questions about the pastimes and characteristics of Lord Vāsudeva,…
reflection: When I speak, hear, or inquire about Vāsudeva-kathā, where do I notice the purification the verse promises — and where do I still walk away unchanged because I was performing the act rather than entering it?

snippet: Once when mother earth was overburdened by hundreds of thousands of military phalanxes of various conceited demons dressed like kings, she approached Lord Brahmā for relief.
reflection: Where in my own life am I, like the demoniac kings of this verse, accumulating 'military phalanxes' — wealth, credentials, defenses, certainties — that burden others and the earth itself rather than serving Kṛṣṇa?

snippet: Mother earth assumed the form of a cow. Very much distressed, with tears in her eyes, she appeared before Lord Brahmā and told him about her misfortune.
reflection: Where in my own life have I, like Bhū-devī, silently borne the weight of others' adharma rather than approaching the proper authority and naming the misfortune plainly?

snippet: Thereafter, having heard of the distress of mother earth, Lord Brahmā, with mother earth, Lord Śiva and all the other demigods, approached the shore of the Ocean of Milk.
reflection: When the 'earth' of my own life is in distress — my health, my family, my work — do I run to my own ingenuity first, or do I, like Brahmā, gather the responsible parties and approach the shore of the Ocean of Milk where the Lord lies?

snippet: After reaching the shore of the Ocean of Milk, the demigods worshiped the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Viṣṇu, the master of the whole universe, the supreme God of all gods, who provides for everyone and…
reflection: Where in my life am I still treating some controller — boss, government, parent, my own intellect — as if they were parameśvara, when SB 10.1.20 calls me to recognize that all such authorities are themselves subordinate to Lord Viṣṇu?

snippet: While in trance, Lord Brahmā heard the words of Lord Viṣṇu vibrating in the sky. Thus he told the demigods: O demigods, hear from me the order of Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu, the Supreme Person, and execute it attentively…
reflection: When the Lord's instructions arrive through the heart in trance, am I sitting still enough — through japa, śravaṇa, and svādhyāya — to actually hear, or is my inner space so crowded with my own commentary that even Brahmā's reception couldn't penetrate?

snippet: Lord Brahmā informed the demigods: Before we submitted our petition to the Lord, He was already aware of the distress on earth. Consequently, for as long as the Lord moves on earth to diminish its burden by His own…
reflection: Where in my life am I assuming Kṛṣṇa is unaware of a burden I am carrying — and what changes the moment I accept that He already knows, before I petition?

snippet: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has full potency, will personally appear as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore all the wives of the demigods should also appear in order to satisfy Him.
reflection: This verse shows that even the sura-strī, residents of the heavenly planets, had to take birth in a particular family at a particular time to be 'fully trained' before going to Goloka — where am I treating my present circumstances (this family, this stage, this duty) as an obstacle to bhakti rather than as the precise training ground Kṛṣṇa has arranged for me?

snippet: The foremost manifestation of Kṛṣṇa is Saṅkarṣaṇa, who is known as Ananta. He is the origin of all incarnations within this material world. Previous to the appearance of Lord Kṛṣṇa, this original Saṅkarṣaṇa will…
reflection: Where in my life am I trying to stand alone in service to Kṛṣṇa, when this verse shows that even the Lord's own expansion appears first to support His pastimes — whose accompanying service have I been refusing to recognize?

snippet: The potency of the Lord, known as viṣṇu-māyā, who is as good as the Supreme Personality of Godhead, will also appear with Lord Kṛṣṇa. This potency, acting in different capacities, captivates all the worlds, both…
reflection: In which areas of my life am I still acting as the ahaṅkāra-vimūḍhātmā — convinced I am the doer — when in fact viṣṇu-māyā is arranging the outcome behind my efforts?

snippet: Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: After thus advising the demigods and pacifying mother earth, the very powerful Lord Brahmā, who is the master of all other Prajāpatis and is therefore known as Prajāpati-pati, returned to…
reflection: Like Brahmā returning to his sva-dhāma after fulfilling his charge, what is the specific post or duty in my own life that I keep stepping away from before the work is actually done — and what reassurance do I owe to those I leave behind?

snippet: Formerly, Śūrasena, the chief of the Yadu dynasty, had gone to live in the city of Mathurā. There he enjoyed the places known as Māthura and Śūrasena.
reflection: Like Śūrasena settling into Mathurā and enjoying his domains, what 'territory' have I quietly settled into and begun to call mine — and what does that ownership conceal about my actual position as a soul passing through?

snippet: Since that time, the city of Mathurā had been the capital of all the kings of the Yadu dynasty. The city and district of Mathurā are very intimately connected with Kṛṣṇa, for Lord Kṛṣṇa lives there eternally.
reflection: If Mathurā and Vṛndāvana are eternally non-different from Kṛṣṇa Himself, what does it reveal about my heart that I treat pilgrimage as tourism — collecting photos and souvenirs — rather than as direct contact with the Lord?

snippet: Some time ago, Vasudeva, who belonged to the demigod family [or to the Śūra dynasty], married Devakī. After the marriage, he mounted his chariot to return home with his newly married wife.
reflection: Vasudeva mounted the chariot with Devakī after a sanctified marriage within the proper varṇāśrama framework — where in my own life have I tried to take a 'chariot ride' (a major life transition: marriage, career, move) without first establishing the dharmic groundwork that Vasudeva did?

snippet: Kaṁsa, the son of King Ugrasena, in order to please his sister Devakī on the occasion of her marriage, took charge of the reins of the horses and became the chariot driver. He was surrounded by hundreds of golden…
reflection: Whose 'wedding chariot' am I currently driving — for whose pleasure am I expending visible effort, and is that affection rooted in service to the soul or only in priya-cikīrṣā for the body?

snippet: Devakī’s father, King Devaka, was very much affectionate to his daughter. Therefore, while she and her husband were leaving home, he gave her a dowry of four hundred elephants nicely decorated with golden garlands.…
reflection: When I give to those I love — children, spouse, family — am I giving in a way befitting my position and capacity, like Devaka, or am I quietly withholding out of attachment to accumulation?

snippet: O beloved son, Mahārāja Parīkṣit, when the bride and bridegroom were ready to start, conchshells, bugles, drums and kettledrums all vibrated in concert for their auspicious departure.
reflection: The conchshells and kettledrums marked a sacred passage from one āśrama into the next — what passage in my own life have I been treating as a logistical event rather than a sumaṅgalam moment worthy of being marked, witnessed, and offered to Kṛṣṇa?

snippet: While Kaṁsa, controlling the reins of the horses, was driving the chariot along the way, an unembodied voice addressed him, “You foolish rascal, the eighth child of the woman you are carrying will kill you!”
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Kaṁsa, receiving clear warnings — from scripture, sādhus, or my own conscience — that I am dismissing as inconvenient noise rather than treating as a turning point?

snippet: Kaṁsa was a condemned personality in the Bhoja dynasty because he was envious and sinful. Therefore, upon hearing this omen from the sky, he caught hold of his sister’s hair with his left hand and took up his sword…
reflection: When my own self-interest feels threatened, whose well-being is the first to drop from my hand — like Kaṁsa dropping the reins to seize his sister's hair — and what does that reveal about the affection I claimed to have?

snippet: Wanting to pacify Kaṁsa, who was so cruel and envious that he was shamelessly ready to kill his sister, the great soul Vasudeva, who was to be the father of Kṛṣṇa, spoke to him in the following words.
reflection: When someone in my life behaves like Kaṁsa — cruel, shameless, threatening what I love — do I meet them with Vasudeva's mahā-bhāga composure, or do I match their agitation and lose the very ground from which I could actually help?

snippet: Vasudeva said: My dear brother-in-law Kaṁsa, you are the pride of your family, the Bhoja dynasty, and great heroes praise your qualities. How could such a qualified person as you kill a woman, your own sister,…
reflection: Where in my own life have I been so consumed by a perceived threat that I, like Kaṁsa, am ready to harm those whom dharma forbids me to touch — a family member, a dependent, someone weaker — and what reasoned appeal of a 'Vasudeva' am I refusing to hear?

snippet: O great hero, one who takes birth is sure to die, for death is born with the body. One may die today or after hundreds of years, but death is sure for every living entity.
reflection: Vasudeva tells Kaṁsa that death is born with the body — where in my own life am I burning energy trying to outrun a death that was sewn into me at birth, instead of using that same energy to prepare for what comes after?

snippet: When the present body turns to dust and is again reduced to five elements — earth, water, fire, air and ether — the proprietor of the body, the living being, automatically receives another body of material elements…
reflection: Which fruitive activities am I currently feeding — through habit, ambition, or indulgence — that are quietly shaping the kind of body and circumstances I will inherit next?

snippet: Just as a person traveling on the road rests one foot on the ground and then lifts the other, or as a worm on a vegetable transfers itself to one leaf and then gives up the previous one, the conditioned soul takes…
reflection: Like the worm that will not release one leaf until its foot is firmly on the next, which body-based identity (role, relationship, possession) am I refusing to release because I have not yet placed my weight on Kṛṣṇa?

snippet: Having experienced a situation by seeing or hearing about it, one contemplates and speculates about that situation, and thus one surrenders to it, not considering his present body. Similarly, by mental adjustments…
reflection: Which 'dream-body' am I currently inhabiting in waking life — what mental rehearsal of a future self, role, or circumstance have I surrendered to, forgetting the body and duty actually in front of me?

snippet: At the time of death, according to the thinking, feeling and willing of the mind, which is involved in fruitive activities, one receives a particular body. In other words, the body develops according to the…
reflection: At the moment of death, the mind I have trained all my life will choose my next body — what mental habit am I cultivating right now that I would be ashamed to wear as a form in my next birth?

snippet: When the luminaries in the sky, such as the moon, the sun and the stars, are reflected in liquids like oil or water, they appear to be of different shapes — sometimes round, sometimes long, and so on — because of the…
reflection: Which 'reflected shape' — a role, nationality, profession, or relationship label — have I been mistaking for my actual self, and what wind of circumstance keeps that reflection moving?

snippet: Therefore, since envious, impious activities cause a body in which one suffers in the next life, why should one act impiously? Considering one’s welfare, one should not envy anyone, for an envious person must always…
reflection: Toward whom am I quietly nursing droha — a coworker, a sibling, an old friend — and what fear of retaliation (in this life or the next) am I refusing to connect to that grudge?

snippet: As your younger sister, this poor girl Devakī is like your own daughter and deserves to be affectionately maintained. You are merciful, and therefore you should not kill her. Indeed, she deserves your affection.
reflection: When someone close to me is in danger or distress, do I appeal to the aggressor's better nature as Vasudeva did with Kaṁsa — or do I retreat into helplessness because the situation feels too volatile to engage?

snippet: Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: O best of the Kuru dynasty, Kaṁsa was fiercely cruel and was actually a follower of the Rākṣasas. Therefore he could be neither pacified nor terrified by the good instructions given by…
reflection: Where in my own life have I, like Kaṁsa, hardened myself against good counsel from someone who genuinely wishes me well — and what rākṣasa-like attachment am I protecting by refusing to listen?

snippet: When Vasudeva saw that Kaṁsa was determined to kill his sister Devakī, he thought to himself very deeply. Considering the imminent danger of death, he thought of another plan to stop Kaṁsa.
reflection: When I face a 'Kaṁsa' in my life — an immovable threat I cannot reason with — do I collapse into helplessness, or do I, like Vasudeva, sit down and think of the next concrete plan?

snippet: As long as he has intelligence and bodily strength, an intelligent person must try to avoid death. This is the duty of every embodied person. But if death cannot be avoided in spite of one’s endeavors, a person…
reflection: Where in my life am I quietly accepting a slow 'death' — of my sādhana, my health, my relationships — without using the buddhi and bala Kṛṣṇa has given me to actively oppose it?

snippet: Vasudeva considered: By delivering all my sons to Kaṁsa, who is death personified, I shall save the life of Devakī. Perhaps Kaṁsa will die before my sons take birth, or, since he is already destined to die at the…
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Vasudeva, negotiating with an immediate threat by promising away something precious in the future — and is this resourcefulness (dākṣya) or quiet cowardice dressed as strategy?

snippet: When a fire, for some unseen reason, leaps over one piece of wood and sets fire to the next, the reason is destiny. Similarly, when a living being accepts one kind of body and leaves aside another, there is no other…
reflection: Where in my life have I been quietly raging against an 'unseen' outcome — a body, a circumstance, a loss — as if I could have engineered it differently with more cleverness or control?

snippet: After thus considering the matter as far as his knowledge would allow, Vasudeva submitted his proposal to the sinful Kaṁsa with great respect.
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Vasudeva, forced to deal respectfully with a 'Kaṁsa' — someone whose intentions I distrust — and is my civility rooted in vinaya for the soul or in fear for my own skin?

snippet: Vasudeva’s mind was full of anxiety because his wife was facing danger, but in order to please the cruel, shameless and sinful Kaṁsa, he externally smiled and spoke to him as follows.
reflection: Where in my life am I confusing duplicity-for-Kṛṣṇa's-purpose with mere self-protection or face-saving — and how can I tell the difference honestly?

snippet: Vasudeva said: O best of the sober, you have nothing to fear from your sister Devakī because of what you have heard from the unseen omen. The cause of death will be her sons. Therefore I promise that when she gives…
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Vasudeva, offering up something precious in advance to appease another's fear — and is that surrender truly skillful service, or quiet capitulation dressed as composure?

snippet: Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Kaṁsa agreed to the logical arguments of Vasudeva, and, having full faith in Vasudeva’s words, he refrained from killing his sister. Vasudeva, being pleased with Kaṁsa, pacified him…
reflection: Whose trust have I quietly squandered by treating my word as negotiable, and what would it cost me today to speak with the unwavering integrity that even a Kaṁsa could rely on?

snippet: Each year thereafter, in due course of time, Devakī, the mother of God and all the demigods, gave birth to a child. Thus she bore eight sons, one after another, and a daughter named Subhadrā.
reflection: When I worship or seek favor from various devas in my life — whether literal demigods or modern equivalents like wealth, health, status — am I bypassing the source (Kṛṣṇa) for the branches, and what does that bypass cost me in real devotional depth?

snippet: Vasudeva was very much disturbed by fear of becoming a liar by breaking his promise. Thus with great pain he delivered his first-born son, named Kīrtimān, into the hands of Kaṁsa.
reflection: Where in my own life am I, like Vasudeva, holding to a promise whose literal fulfillment seems to harm what I most love — and what does keeping my word in the face of that pain ask of me today?

snippet: What is painful for saintly persons who strictly adhere to the truth? How could there not be independence for pure devotees who know the Supreme Lord as the substance? What deeds are forbidden for persons of the…
reflection: When I say something is 'too painful' or 'impossible' to bear, what does that confession reveal about where I have placed my identity — in the body and its comforts, or in the soul's relationship with Kṛṣṇa?

snippet: My dear King Parīkṣit, when Kaṁsa saw that Vasudeva, being situated in truthfulness, was completely equipoised in giving him the child, he was very happy. Therefore, with a smiling face, he spoke as follows.
reflection: Where in my life do I confuse emotional flatness or numbness with the samatvam Vasudeva displayed — and how would I tell the difference between true equipoise rooted in surrender to Kṛṣṇa and simple suppression?

snippet: O Vasudeva, you may take back your child and go home. I have no fear of your first child. It is the eighth child of you and Devakī I am concerned with because that is the child by whom I am destined to be killed.
reflection: Kaṁsa shows chilling daksya in calculating exactly which child threatens him — where in my own life am I deploying real skill and resourcefulness toward a self-protective scheme rather than toward sva-dharma?

snippet: Vasudeva agreed and took his child back home, but because Kaṁsa had no character and no self-control, Vasudeva knew that he could not rely on Kaṁsa’s word.
reflection: Whose word am I currently relying on — at home, in friendship, or in study — that the evidence of their character (asato 'vijitātmanaḥ) has already told me cannot be trusted, and what is my attachment to believing them?

snippet: The inhabitants of Vṛndāvana, headed by Nanda Mahārāja and including his associate cowherd men and their wives, were none but denizens of the heavenly planets, O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, best of the descendants of Bharata,…
reflection: This verse reveals that even those who 'externally appeared to be followers of Kaṁsa' were demigods playing a part in Kṛṣṇa's pastimes — where in my own life have I judged someone as an obstacle when they may actually be an instrument in a larger arrangement I cannot see?

snippet: Once the great saint Nārada approached Kaṁsa and informed him of how the demoniac persons who were a great burden on the earth were going to be killed. Thus Kaṁsa was placed into great fear and doubt.
reflection: Nārada's warning placed Kaṁsa in fear because his whole life was built on demoniac premises — where in my own life would a clear word from a sādhu about Kṛṣṇa's coming provoke fear rather than joy, and what does that fear reveal about what I am still protecting?

snippet: After the departure of the great saint Nārada, Kaṁsa thought that all the members of the Yadu dynasty were demigods and that any of the children born from the womb of Devakī might be Viṣṇu. Fearing his death, Kaṁsa…
reflection: Kaṁsa believed that by killing each newborn he could outwit a prophecy from the Lord — where in my own life am I expending enormous effort to control an outcome that is not actually mine to determine?

snippet: Kings greedy for sense gratification on this earth almost always kill their enemies indiscriminately. To satisfy their own whims, they may kill anyone, even their mothers, fathers, brothers or friends.
reflection: Where in my own life have I quietly justified harming someone close to me — in word, withheld attention, or broken trust — because some 'whim' of mine (status, comfort, ambition) demanded it?

snippet: In his previous birth, Kaṁsa had been a great demon named Kālanemi and been killed by Viṣṇu. Upon learning this information from Nārada, Kaṁsa became envious of everyone connected with the Yadu dynasty.
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Kaṁsa, nursing an old grievance — treating someone connected to a past wound as an enemy today, rather than seeing them as a soul before me?

snippet: Kaṁsa, the most powerful son of Ugrasena, even imprisoned his own father, the King of the Yadu, Bhoja and Andhaka dynasties, and personally ruled the states known as Śūrasena.
reflection: Like Kaṁsa imprisoning his own father Ugrasena to seize the throne, what rightful authority in my life — a parent, a teacher, a guru, my own conscience — have I quietly 'imprisoned' or sidelined so I can rule unchecked over my own little Śūrasena?

snippet: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Under the protection of Magadharāja, Jarāsandha, the powerful Kaṁsa began persecuting the kings of the Yadu dynasty. In this he had the cooperation of demons like Pralamba, Baka, Cāṇūra,…
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Kaṁsa, taking shelter of a 'Jarāsandha' — some powerful worldly alliance, ideology, or institution — to legitimize a course of action I already sense is opposed to Kṛṣṇa's purpose?

snippet: Persecuted by the demoniac kings, the Yādavas left their own kingdom and entered various others, like those of the Kurus, Pañcālas, Kekayas, Śālvas, Vidarbhas, Niṣadhas, Videhas and Kośalas.
reflection: When my own 'kingdom' — my routine, my settled life — is disturbed by hostile pressure, do I read it as senseless persecution, or am I willing to consider it as Kṛṣṇa's arrangement to relocate me toward where He wants me?

snippet: Some of their relatives, however, began to follow Kaṁsa’s principles and act in his service. After Kaṁsa, the son of Ugrasena, killed the six sons of Devakī, a plenary portion of Kṛṣṇa entered her womb as her seventh…
reflection: Like Akrūra remaining in Kaṁsa's court to witness Kṛṣṇa's appearance, where am I being asked to stay inside an uncomfortable or compromising situation — not to serve it, but to be present for the Lord's work that will unfold there?

snippet: To protect the Yadus, His personal devotees, from Kaṁsa’s attack, the Personality of Godhead, Viśvātmā, the Supreme Soul of everyone, ordered Yoga-māyā as follows.
reflection: Where in my life have I been trying to protect myself through my own arrangements, instead of crying out to Kṛṣṇa as Devakī did and trusting that He will dispatch Yoga-māyā on my behalf?

snippet: The Lord ordered Yoga-māyā: O My potency, who are worshipable for the entire world and whose nature is to bestow good fortune upon all living entities, go to Vraja, where there live many cowherd men and their wives.…
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Vasudeva's other wives, hiding in 'caves' out of fear of some Kaṁsa — a person, an outcome, a worldly threat — instead of trusting Kṛṣṇa's arrangement to place me where I truly need to be?

snippet: Within the womb of Devakī is My partial plenary expansion known as Saṅkarṣaṇa or Śeṣa. Without difficulty, transfer Him into the womb of Rohiṇī.
reflection: Which 'asuras' — kāma, krodha, lobha, moha, mada, mātsarya — is still gestating in the womb of my consciousness, and what specific material association keeps feeding it?

snippet: O all-auspicious Yoga-māyā, I shall then appear with My full six opulences as the son of Devakī, and you will appear as the daughter of mother Yaśodā, the queen of Mahārāja Nanda.
reflection: Where in my life am I trying to act as the sole 'doer' — when in truth, like Yoga-māyā needing Kṛṣṇa's śubhe blessing to attract Saṅkarṣaṇa, I am only a part being moved by His potency?

snippet: By sacrifices of animals, ordinary human beings will worship you gorgeously, with various paraphernalia, because you are supreme in fulfilling the material desires of everyone.
reflection: Which 'sarva-kāma' — which bundle of material desires — am I quietly hoping the spiritual path will fulfill, rather than dissolve?

snippet: Lord Kṛṣṇa blessed Māyādevī by saying: In different places on the surface of the earth, people will give you different names, such as Durgā, Bhadrakālī, Vijayā, Vaiṣṇavī, Kumudā, Caṇḍikā, Kṛṣṇā, Mādhavī, Kanyakā,…
reflection: Under which of Māyādevī's many names — security, beauty, prestige, family safety, intellectual mastery — am I most comfortably worshiping the material energy while telling myself I am being spiritual?

snippet: The son of Rohiṇī will also be celebrated as Saṅkarṣaṇa because of being sent from the womb of Devakī to the womb of Rohiṇī. He will be called Rāma because of His ability to please all the inhabitants of Gokula, and…
reflection: Balarāma is called Rāma because He pleases all the inhabitants of Gokula (loka-ramaṇāt) — whose joy am I actually organizing my day around, and whose joy do I quietly resent having to consider?

snippet: Thus instructed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Yoga-māyā immediately agreed. With the Vedic mantra om, she confirmed that she would do what He asked. Thus having accepted the order of the Supreme Personality…
reflection: When the Lord — through guru, śāstra, or sādhu — gives me a clear instruction, where do I delay, negotiate, or 'think it over' instead of responding with Yoga-māyā's immediate 'tathā' and 'om'?

snippet: When the child of Devakī was attracted and transferred into the womb of Rohiṇī by Yoga-māyā, Devakī seemed to have a miscarriage. Thus all the inhabitants of the palace loudly lamented, “Alas, Devakī has lost her child!”
reflection: Where in my own life have I mistaken Yoga-māyā's protective rearrangement for loss — what 'miscarriage' did I once mourn that was actually Kṛṣṇa's hand quietly relocating something for safekeeping?

snippet: Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the Supersoul of all living entities and who vanquishes all the fear of His devotees, entered the mind of Vasudeva in full opulence.
reflection: Vasudeva became a fit vessel because his consciousness was purified — where in my own mind is Kṛṣṇa being crowded out by viṣaya, and what concretely would I have to clear so that He could 'enter' there?

snippet: While carrying the form of the Supreme Personality of Godhead within the core of his heart, Vasudeva bore the Lord’s transcendentally illuminating effulgence, and thus he became as bright as the sun. He was therefore…
reflection: What in my life — a service, a responsibility, a relationship — am I empowered by Kṛṣṇa to carry, and am I bearing it with the gravitas of a dhāma or treating it as merely my own clever doing?

snippet: Thereafter, accompanied by plenary expansions, the fully opulent Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is all-auspicious for the entire universe, was transferred from the mind of Vasudeva to the mind of Devakī. Devakī,…
reflection: Whose heart am I actually drawing Kṛṣṇa from — am I trying to 'meditate Him up' on my own, or am I receiving Him through a bona fide channel of dīkṣā?

snippet: Devakī then kept within herself the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the cause of all causes, the foundation of the entire cosmos, but because she was under arrest in the house of Kaṁsa, she was like the flames of a…
reflection: What kṛṣṇa-conscious knowledge has Kṛṣṇa already placed within me — through hearing, reading, or association — that I am keeping 'arrested in the Bhojendra-gehe' of my private life instead of distributing to those around me?

snippet: Because the Supreme Personality of Godhead was within her womb, Devakī illuminated the entire atmosphere in the place where she was confined. Seeing her jubilant, pure and smiling, Kaṁsa thought, “The Supreme…
reflection: Devakī's tejas radiated outward because Kṛṣṇa was within her — what 'inner cargo' am I currently carrying (entertainment, anxieties, calculations) that is silently radiating from me and shaping how others perceive me?

snippet: Kaṁsa thought: What is my duty now? The Supreme Lord, who knows His purpose will not give up His prowess. Devakī is a woman, she is my sister, and moreover she is now pregnant. If I kill her, my reputation, opulence…
reflection: Like Kaṁsa, where am I restraining a harmful act not out of karuṇā for the soul but only to protect my own yaśas, śrī, and āyuḥ — and what does that reveal about whose welfare I am actually serving?

snippet: A person who is very cruel is regarded as dead even while living, for while he is living or after his death, everyone condemns him. And after the death of a person in the bodily concept of life, he is undoubtedly…
reflection: Where in my life am I a tanu-mānī — identifying so completely with this body, family, community, or nation that I am quietly accumulating the very karma that leads to Andhatama?

snippet: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Deliberating in this way, Kaṁsa, although determined to continue in enmity toward the Supreme Personality of Godhead, refrained from the vicious killing of his sister. He decided to wait until…
reflection: Like Kaṁsa, where am I postponing a confrontation with what I know I must surrender — telling myself I'll deal with Kṛṣṇa 'when He arrives' rather than today?

snippet: While sitting on his throne or in his sitting room, while lying on his bed, or, indeed, while situated anywhere, and while eating, sleeping or walking, Kaṁsa saw only his enemy, the Supreme Lord, Hṛṣīkeśa. In other…
reflection: Like Kaṁsa, where in my day am I 'unfavorably Kṛṣṇa conscious' — fixated on someone or something I resent, so that even while sitting, eating, and walking, my mind orbits that object instead of Hṛṣīkeśa?

snippet: Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva, accompanied by great sages like Nārada, Devala and Vyāsa and by other demigods like Indra, Candra and Varuṇa, invisibly approached the room of Devakī, where they all joined in offering…
reflection: Brahmā, Śiva, and Nārada — beings of vast cosmic stature — set aside their posts to invisibly approach Devakī's room and offer prayers. Where in my life do I quietly assume I am 'too senior,' too capable, or too busy to take the lower seat before Kṛṣṇa and His devotees?

snippet: The demigods prayed: O Lord, You never deviate from Your vow, which is always perfect because whatever You decide is perfectly correct and cannot be stopped by anyone. Being present in the three phases of cosmic…
reflection: Where in my life am I quietly seeking shelter in 'relative truths' — career security, relationships, health routines, savings — as if they were satya, when this verse insists only Kṛṣṇa is satyasya satyam?

snippet: The body [the total body and the individual body are of the same composition] may figuratively be called “the original tree.” From this tree, which fully depends on the ground of material nature, come two kinds of…
reflection: Of the four 'tastes' of bodily fruit — dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa — which one am I most quietly chasing as if it were the goal, forgetting that it's still just a fruit on the tree of the body?

snippet: The efficient cause of this material world, manifested with its many varieties as the original tree, is You, O Lord. You are also the maintainer of this material world, and after annihilation You are the one in whom…
reflection: Where in my life am I still attributing credit, blame, or causation to 'demigods' — boss, market, body, government — instead of seeing Kṛṣṇa as the single source, maintainer, and reservoir behind all of it?

snippet: O Lord, You are always in full knowledge, and to bring all good fortune to all living entities, You appear in different incarnations, all of them transcendental to the material creation. When You appear in these…
reflection: Where in my life am I quietly hoping Kṛṣṇa will arrange the 'sukha-āvaha' outcome for me, while resisting the abhadra He may need to send to annihilate the duṣkṛti tendencies I am still feeding?

snippet: O lotus-eyed Lord, by concentrating one’s meditation on Your lotus feet, which are the reservoir of all existence, and by accepting those lotus feet as the boat by which to cross the ocean of nescience, one follows…
reflection: Whose footsteps am I actually following right now — a recognized mahājana in the paramparā, or some self-styled authority I picked because they flatter my existing direction?

snippet: O Lord, who resemble the shining sun, You are always ready to fulfill the desire of Your devotee, and therefore You are known as a desire tree [vāñchā-kalpataru]. When ācāryas completely take shelter under Your lotus…
reflection: Which method left behind by the ācāryas — the books, the four regulative principles, the sixteen rounds — am I quietly editing down to suit my convenience, and what does that edit reveal about my unwillingness to actually cross the bhavārṇava?

snippet: [Someone may say that aside from devotees, who always seek shelter at the Lord’s lotus feet, there are those who are not devotees but who have accepted different processes for attaining salvation. What happens to…
reflection: Where in my life am I working hard at some 'process' — career climb, self-improvement project, even a spiritual technique — while quietly neglecting Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, and what does that neglect actually look like in my daily hours?

snippet: O Mādhava, Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord of the goddess of fortune, if devotees completely in love with You sometimes fall from the path of devotion, they do not fall like nondevotees, for You still protect…
reflection: Where am I quietly presuming on Mādhava's protection — using 'a devotee never perishes' as license to take shortcuts in sādhana I would never tolerate in a fellow practitioner?

snippet: O Lord, during the time of maintenance You manifest several incarnations, all with transcendental bodies, beyond the material modes of nature. When You appear in this way, You bestow all good fortune upon the living…
reflection: Which of my daily duties — work, study, family obligations — am I performing without any conscious sense that they are an offering to Kṛṣṇa, and what would change today if I added that intention?

snippet: O Lord, cause of all causes, if Your transcendental body were not beyond the modes of material nature, one could not understand the difference between matter and transcendence. Only by Your presence can one…
reflection: Where am I quietly manufacturing my own version of Kṛṣṇa — fitting Him into the mode of nature I happen to be comfortable with — instead of receiving Him as Brahmā and the ācāryas have presented Him?

snippet: O Lord, Your transcendental name and form are not ascertained by those who merely speculate on the path of imagination. Your name, form and attributes can be ascertained only through devotional service.
reflection: Where in my study of Kṛṣṇa am I still relying on intellectual speculation and 'mental imagination' rather than the sevonmukha attitude this verse insists is the only door?

snippet: Even while engaged in various activities, devotees whose minds are completely absorbed at Your lotus feet, and who constantly hear, chant, contemplate and cause others to remember Your transcendental names and forms,…
reflection: Across the activities that fill my day — work, errands, meals, conversations — where does my consciousness actually rest, and what would it take to relocate it at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet without abandoning the activity itself?

snippet: O Lord, we are fortunate because the heavy burden of the demons upon this earth is immediately removed by Your appearance. Indeed, we are certainly fortunate, for we shall be able to see upon this earth and in the…
reflection: The demigods rejoiced not only that the burden of demons would be lifted, but that they would now see Kṛṣṇa's footprints on the earth — where in my own life am I more eager for relief from problems than for the actual darśana of the Lord's presence?

snippet: O Supreme Lord, You are not an ordinary living entity appearing in this material world as a result of fruitive activities. Therefore Your appearance or birth in this world has no other cause than Your pleasure…
reflection: Where in my life am I still arguing — like the philosophers Prabhupāda names — that Kṛṣṇa 'should not' descend, by quietly insisting my situation is too ordinary, too broken, or too late for His personal intervention?

snippet: O supreme controller, Your Lordship previously accepted incarnations as a fish, a horse, a tortoise, Narasiṁhadeva, a boar, a swan, Lord Rāmacandra, Paraśurāma and, among the demigods, Vāmanadeva, to protect the…
reflection: When I face a disturbance in my world, do I instinctively try to manage it myself, or do I bow down and pray for Kṛṣṇa's intervention as the demigods did here — and what does my reflex reveal about whom I actually trust?

snippet: O mother Devakī, by your good fortune and ours, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself, with all His plenary portions, such as Baladeva, is now within your womb. Therefore you need not fear Kaṁsa, who has decided…
reflection: Where in my life am I still bracing against a 'Kaṁsa' — some looming threat — as if Kṛṣṇa were not already present within the situation as its eventual protector?

snippet: After thus offering prayers to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Viṣṇu, the Transcendence, all the demigods, with Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva before them, returned to their homes in the heavenly planets.
reflection: The demigods perceived Kṛṣṇa's appearance because, as the purport says, they were 'fortunate' devotees — where in my own life am I treating spiritual perception as a matter of cleverness or effort rather than the bhāgya that comes from sincere service?

snippet: Thereafter, at the auspicious time for the appearance of the Lord, the entire universe was surcharged with all the qualities of goodness, beauty and peace. The constellation Rohiṇī appeared, as did stars like Aśvinī.…
reflection: The whole cosmos arranged itself in sattva to receive Kṛṣṇa — what disturbances in my own inner atmosphere (the rajas and tamas in my mind, speech, and habits) am I tolerating that would have to settle for me to actually receive Him today?

snippet: The Kinnaras and Gandharvas began to sing auspicious songs, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas offered auspicious prayers, and the Vidyādharīs, along with the Apsarās, began to dance in jubilation.
reflection: When Kṛṣṇa truly enters my life — through sādhana, through service, through a moment of His mercy — do I respond with the spontaneous jubilation of the Gandharvas and Apsarās, or do I let my ahaṅkāra keep the celebration muted and private?

snippet: The demigods and great saintly persons showered flowers in a joyous mood, and clouds gathered in the sky and very mildly thundered, making sounds like those of the ocean’s waves. Then the Supreme Personality of…
reflection: Where in my life am I still relating to Kṛṣṇa as an 'ordinary child' of history — admiring His story but not trusting that the same antaryāmī is in the core of my own heart right now?

snippet: Vasudeva then saw the newborn child, who had very wonderful lotuslike eyes and who bore in His four hands the four weapons śaṅkha, cakra, gadā and padma. On His chest was the mark of Śrīvatsa and on His neck the…
reflection: When I encounter Kṛṣṇa's four-armed, ornamented form in this verse, what part of me wants to file it away as 'mythology' rather than receive it as the literal descent of the Supreme — and what is that resistance protecting?

snippet: When Vasudeva saw his extraordinary son, his eyes were struck with wonder. In transcendental jubilation, he mentally collected ten thousand cows and distributed them among the brāhmaṇas as a transcendental festival.
reflection: Vasudeva was imprisoned and could not stage an external festival, so he performed yajña entirely within his mind — what offering to Kṛṣṇa have I been postponing because my outer circumstances feel too constrained, when the mental act would already be 'as good'?

snippet: O Mahārāja Parīkṣit, descendant of King Bharata, Vasudeva could understand that this child was the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa. Having concluded this without a doubt, he became fearless. Bowing down with…
reflection: Where in my life am I still trying to offer prayers and surrender from a posture of fear, instead of letting prabhāva-vit — recognition of Kṛṣṇa's protective influence — make me gata-bhīḥ?

snippet: Vasudeva said: My Lord, You are the Supreme Person, beyond material existence, and You are the Supersoul. Your form can be perceived by transcendental knowledge, by which You can be understood as the Supreme…
reflection: Where in my life am I still relating to Kṛṣṇa as if He were a small, vulnerable presence I must protect with my own intelligence — instead of recognizing Him as puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ, beyond the very anxieties I am projecting onto Him?

snippet: My Lord, You are the same person who in the beginning created this material world by His personal external energy. After the creation of this world of three guṇas [sattva, rajas and tamas], You appear to have entered…
reflection: Where in my life am I treating Kṛṣṇa as 'limited' to a particular form, role, or moment — failing to see Him as simultaneously within and beyond every situation I face today?

snippet: The mahat-tattva, the total material energy, is undivided, but because of the material modes of nature, it appears to separate into earth, water, fire, air and ether. Because of the living energy [jīva-bhūta], these…
reflection: Where am I still treating Kṛṣṇa as one more 'thing' my senses must verify before I trust Him — and what would change today if I accepted that He is already inside and outside the situation I am trying to control?

snippet: One who considers his visible body, which is a product of the three modes of nature, to be independent of the soul is unaware of the basis of existence, and therefore he is a rascal. Those who are learned have…
reflection: Where am I quietly behaving as if my body is independent of the soul — decorating it, fearing for it, identifying with it — even though I would never say so aloud?

snippet: O my Lord, learned Vedic scholars conclude that the creation, maintenance and annihilation of the entire cosmic manifestation are performed by You, who are free from endeavor, unaffected by the modes of material…
reflection: Where in my life am I straining and 'endeavoring' as if I were the doer, when the verse says even the cosmos itself unfolds under Kṛṣṇa's effortless glance — what would it look like to act today as His instrument rather than as the proprietor of outcomes?

snippet: My Lord, Your form is transcendental to the three material modes, yet for the maintenance of the three worlds, You assume the white color of Viṣṇu in goodness; for creation, which is surrounded by the quality of…
reflection: Where in my life am I mistaking the colors of the guṇas — the moods of sattva, rajas, or tamas passing through me — for my actual identity, and what would change if I held them as Kṛṣṇa's potencies rather than as 'me'?

snippet: O my Lord, proprietor of all creation, You have now appeared in my house, desiring to protect this world. I am sure that You will kill all the armies that are moving all over the world under the leadership of…
reflection: Where in my own life am I tolerating 'asuras dressed as kṣatriyas' — leaders, voices, or influences I follow because they wear the costume of authority, even though they are leading me away from Kṛṣṇa?

snippet: O my Lord, Lord of the demigods, after hearing the prophecy that You would take birth in our home and kill him, this uncivilized Kaṁsa killed so many of Your elder brothers. As soon as he hears from his lieutenants…
reflection: Where in my life have I been quietly behaving like Kaṁsa — sacrificing innocents (people, principles, time, integrity) for the sake of my own sense-gratification or self-preservation, and what 'prophecy' am I trying to outrun?

snippet: Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued: Thereafter, having seen that her child had all the symptoms of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Devakī, who was very much afraid of Kaṁsa and unusually astonished, began to offer…
reflection: Where in my devotional life do I, like Devakī, intellectually know Kṛṣṇa is supreme yet still tremble for Him as if He needed my protection from the 'Kaṁsas' of the world?

snippet: Śrī Devakī said: My dear Lord, there are different Vedas, some of which describe You as unperceivable through words and the mind. Yet You are the origin of the entire cosmic manifestation. You are Brahman, the…
reflection: Where in my life am I quietly worshiping a 'demigod' — career, health, relationship, ideology — as if it were an independent source of refuge, when this verse insists every such shelter is only borrowed effulgence from Kṛṣṇa Himself?

snippet: After millions of years, at the time of cosmic annihilation, when everything, manifested and unmanifested, is annihilated by the force of time, the five gross elements enter into the subtle conception, and the…
reflection: When I picture the dvi-parārdha dissolution — every gross element folding back into the unmanifest, every category I rely on for identity erased — what part of my present self-conception cannot survive that contraction, and why am I still investing in it?

snippet: O inaugurator of the material energy, this wonderful creation works under the control of powerful time, which is divided into seconds, minutes, hours and years. This element of time, which extends for many millions…
reflection: Where in my life am I still pretending to be the controller of time — scheduling, planning, gripping outcomes — when this verse names Kṛṣṇa Himself as the One who moves the cosmic wheel?

snippet: No one in this material world has become free from the four principles birth, death, old age and disease, even by fleeing to various planets. But now that You have appeared, My Lord, death is fleeing in fear of You,…
reflection: To which 'higher planet' — promotion, security, longevity, even a spiritual achievement — am I still fleeing in the hope it will exempt me from death, instead of taking shelter at Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet?

snippet: My Lord, because You dispel all the fear of Your devotees, I request You to save us and give us protection from the terrible fear of Kaṁsa. Your form as Viṣṇu, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is appreciated by…
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Devakī, asking Kṛṣṇa to 'tone down' His full presence because His undisguised reality threatens the safety I have built around a 'Kaṁsa' I still fear?

snippet: O Madhusūdana, because of Your appearance, I am becoming more and more anxious in fear of Kaṁsa. Therefore, please arrange for that sinful Kaṁsa to be unable to understand that You have taken birth from my womb.
reflection: Where, like Devakī, has my affection for what I love made me forget Kṛṣṇa's unlimited power — and start treating Him as something I must protect rather than surrender to?

snippet: O my Lord, You are the all-pervading Supreme Personality of Godhead, and Your transcendental four-armed form, holding conchshell, disc, club and lotus, is unnatural for this world. Please withdraw this form [and…
reflection: Where in my sādhana am I, like Devakī, secretly asking Kṛṣṇa to dim His majesty so that I can fit Him into a life I have already arranged on my own terms?

snippet: At the time of devastation, the entire cosmos, containing all created moving and nonmoving entities, enters Your transcendental body and is held there without difficulty. But now this transcendental form has taken…
reflection: Where in my devotional life am I, like Devakī, quietly asking Kṛṣṇa to dim His opulence so that He fits within what my social world will accept?

snippet: The Supreme Personality of Godhead replied: My dear mother, best of the chaste, in your previous birth, in the Svāyambhuva millennium, you were known as Pṛśni, and Vasudeva, who was the most pious Prajāpati, was…
reflection: Where in my life am I treating my relationships — especially with parents, children, or spouse — as merely material accidents, when this verse insists Kṛṣṇa Himself selects His eternal associates across yugas?

snippet: When both of you were ordered by Lord Brahmā to create progeny, you first underwent severe austerities by controlling your senses.
reflection: Where in my own life am I trying to 'mechanically control' an outcome — through technique, willpower, or arrangement — when the verse points to tapas and indriya-saṁyama as the real preparation?

snippet: My dear father and mother, you endured rain, wind, strong sun, scorching heat and severe cold, suffering all sorts of inconvenience according to different seasons. By practicing prāṇāyāma to control the air within…
reflection: Pṛśni and Sutapā endured rain, sun, scorching heat, and cold to clear the dirt from their minds — what specific seasonal discomfort or bodily inconvenience am I currently rearranging my whole life to escape, and what mental dirt is that avoidance protecting?

snippet: Thus you spent twelve thousand celestial years performing difficult activities of tapasya in consciousness of Me [Kṛṣṇa consciousness].
reflection: Twelve thousand celestial years of tapas were sustained by mad-ātmanoḥ — consciousness fixed on Kṛṣṇa. Where in my own sādhana do I rely on willpower or self-image to endure austerity, instead of letting consciousness of Him be the sustaining force?

snippet: O sinless mother Devakī, after the expiry of twelve thousand celestial years, in which you constantly contemplated Me within the core of your heart with great faith, devotion and austerity, I was very much satisfied…
reflection: Sutapā and Pṛśni performed twelve thousand celestial years of tapas just to have the Lord come down as their son — what am I attempting to drag Kṛṣṇa into my world to obtain, instead of letting Him draw me back to His?

snippet: Being husband and wife but always sonless, you were attracted by sexual desires, for by the influence of devamāyā, transcendental love, you wanted to have Me as your son. Therefore you never desired to be liberated…
reflection: Where in my life am I dressing up a material attachment as a spiritual aspiration — wanting Kṛṣṇa to enter my situation rather than wanting to leave the situation for Him?

snippet: After you received that benediction and I disappeared, you engaged yourselves in sex to have a son like Me, and I fulfilled your desire.
reflection: Where in my life am I treating a benediction from Kṛṣṇa as license for grāmya-bhoga — using a spiritual gift to ratify a material craving I had not yet renounced?

snippet: Since I found no one else as highly elevated as you in simplicity and other qualities of good character, I appeared in this world as Pṛśnigarbha, or one who is celebrated as having taken birth from Pṛśni.
reflection: Where in my life do I posture with elaborate qualities while quietly lacking the simple, straightforward śīla and ārjava that actually drew the Lord to Pṛśni and Sutapā?

snippet: In the next millennium, I again appeared from the two of you, who appeared as My mother, Aditi, and My father, Kaśyapa. I was known as Upendra, and because of being a dwarf, I was also known as Vāmana.
reflection: Where in my life am I refusing to 'become small' — like Vāmana — to recover what has been usurped, insisting instead that my full stature be acknowledged before I act?

snippet: O supremely chaste mother, I, the same personality, have now appeared of you both as your son for the third time. Take My words as the truth.
reflection: Where in my life am I treating Kṛṣṇa as a partial expansion — useful for some needs, kept at a distance for others — instead of receiving Him in His full opulence as Sutapā and Pṛśni did?

snippet: I have shown you this form of Viṣṇu just to remind you of My previous births. Otherwise, if I appeared like an ordinary human child, you would not believe that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, has indeed…
reflection: Where in my sādhana am I quietly demanding that Kṛṣṇa show me a four-armed Viṣṇu form before I will trust Him — refusing to recognize Him in the 'ordinary human child' shape He has actually given me (the holy name, the Deity, the words of the ācārya)?

snippet: Both of you, husband and wife, constantly think of Me as your son, but always know that I am the Supreme Personality of Godhead. By thus thinking of Me constantly with love and affection, you will achieve the highest…
reflection: Where in my life am I treating Kṛṣṇa as merely a sweet, near presence (like a son or friend) while quietly forgetting He is the Supreme Personality of Godhead — and where am I doing the reverse, holding Him at a distance as 'the Absolute' to avoid the intimacy of personal love?

snippet: Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After thus instructing His father and mother, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, remained silent. In their presence, by His internal energy, He then transformed Himself into a small…
reflection: Where in my life do I quietly insist that Kṛṣṇa must conform to my human categories — and what would it cost my pride to admit His ātma-māyā is beyond my mind's reach?

snippet: Thereafter, exactly when Vasudeva, being inspired by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, was about to take the newborn child from the delivery room, Yoga-māyā, the Lord’s spiritual energy, took birth as the daughter…

snippet: By the influence of Yoga-māyā, all the doorkeepers fell fast asleep, their senses unable to work, and the other inhabitants of the house also fell deeply asleep. When the sun rises, the darkness automatically…
reflection: What 'iron-bolted doors' in my own life have I been straining to force open through willpower, when the verse suggests the real work is to carry Kṛṣṇa first and let the obstacles open of themselves?

snippet: Because of constant rain sent by the demigod Indra, the river Yamunā was filled with deep water, foaming about with fiercely whirling waves. But as the great Indian Ocean had formerly given way to Lord Rāmacandra by…
reflection: When the 'Yamunā' of my circumstances rises against me — opposition, delay, fear — do I read it as Kṛṣṇa's obstacle or as nature itself parting for the service He has entrusted to me?

reflection: Where in my life am I, like Vasudeva, quietly carrying out a duty that looks harsh on the surface but is actually being moved by a deeper providence — and have I had the honesty to recognize Yoga-māyā's hand in it rather than crediting my own cleverness?

snippet: Vasudeva placed the female child on the bed of Devakī, bound his legs with the iron shackles, and thus remained there as before.
reflection: Where in my life am I, like Vasudeva, voluntarily putting the shackles back on after the gates have opened — and what fear of being seen as 'free' am I protecting?

reflection: Where in my life am I playing the doglike watchman — barking in alarm at events Yoga-māyā has already arranged, mistaking my reactivity for responsibility?

snippet: My lord, my brother, I am very poor, being bereft of all my children, but still I am your younger sister, and therefore it would be worthy of you to give me this last child as a gift.

reflection: Where in my own life am I, like Kaṁsa, snatching from another's hands what I am terrified of losing — and calling that decisiveness?

snippet: Having uprooted all relationships with his sister because of intense selfishness, Kaṁsa, who was sitting on his knees, grasped the newborn child by the legs and tried to dash her against the surface of a stone.
reflection: Where in my life have I, like Kaṁsa, allowed sva-artha (selfish interest) to silently uproot a sauhṛda — a bond of natural affection — and called it pragmatism?

snippet: The child, Yoga-māyā-devī, the younger sister of Lord Viṣṇu, slipped upward from Kaṁsa’s hands and appeared in the sky as Devī, the goddess Durgā, with eight arms, completely equipped with weapons.

snippet: O great souls, your children have suffered their own misfortune. Therefore, please do not lament for them. All living entities are under the control of the Supreme, and they cannot always live together.

snippet: Kaṁsa begged, “My dear sister and brother-in-law, please be merciful to such a poor-hearted person as me, since both of you are saintly persons. Please excuse my atrocities.” Having said this, Kaṁsa fell at the feet…
